cluster_summary: A collection of vulnerabilities where protocol parsers (HTTP, email, AJP, etc.) fail to validate user-supplied input for control characters, enforce protocol-specific constraints, or limit resource consumption, leading to CRLF injection, request smuggling, denial of service, or email header manipulation.
guideline_text: Trace attacker-controlled webhook URLs, callback URLs, endpoint parameters, or request destinations into outbound HTTP clients, URL.openConnection, fetch helpers, proxy clients, or webhook dispatchers. Report code paths where scheme, host, redirect target, DNS resolution, and private-address ranges are not constrained before the outbound request. Confirm that the required guard is enforced on the same source-to-sink path before the sensitive effect. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 3 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should enforce scheme and host allowlists, block private and metadata addresses after DNS resolution, and validate redirect targets.

mechanism.missing_guard: scheme, host, redirect target, DNS resolution, and private-address ranges are not constrained before the outbound request
mechanism.name: attacker-controlled webhook or callback URL fetch
mechanism.sink_shape: outbound HTTP clients, URL.openConnection, fetch helpers, proxy clients, or webhook dispatchers
mechanism.source_shape: attacker-controlled webhook URLs, callback URLs, endpoint parameters, or request destinations
mechanism.typical_fix: enforce scheme and host allowlists, block private and metadata addresses after DNS resolution, and validate redirect targets

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Add validation to reject or strip CR/LF characters in header values, either by enabling built-in validation (e.g., DefaultHttpHeaders with validation) or by adding explicit character checks before header construction.
sub_patterns.name: CRLF injection due to missing header value validation
sub_patterns.root_cause: The code assumes that user-controlled header values are safe and does not sanitize or reject carriage return (\r) and line feed (\n) characters before inserting them into protocol headers (HTTP, SSE, SMTP, etc.).

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Introduce configurable limits (e.g., maxFields, maxBytes, maxHeaders), use efficient algorithms (e.g., O(n log n) sort), and track cumulative sizes incrementally to prevent resource exhaustion.
sub_patterns.name: Resource exhaustion due to missing limits in input parsing
sub_patterns.root_cause: The parser does not impose limits on the number of fields, field sizes, buffer sizes, or algorithmic complexity, allowing an attacker to cause unbounded memory or CPU consumption.

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Add byte-level validation using a ByteProcessor to reject any byte not in the allowed set before converting to string.
sub_patterns.name: Missing character validation in binary HTTP parser
sub_patterns.root_cause: The binary HTTP parser does not validate that bytes in method, scheme, authority, and path fields are valid HTTP tokens or scheme characters, allowing injection of whitespace or control characters.
